items.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: He was the musical director for the Arsenio Hall show.

ctx.x: Did you have a name for it or did you let other people name it?

We just let other people name it. We just called it — it was just music for us you know. We didn’t want to be in one particular slot all the time, like just straight ahead jazz or something. We wanted to be able to do all kinds of things and have some fun. And not only did we do different like Funk and Soul and Gospel and Jazz, we also experimented with different time figures and things too at that time. Like seven-four time, five-four time and things like that, which were, we did “Seventy Four Miles Away” that…
And he was with Blood, Sweat and Tears too wasn’t he, later on?
